case.title: App stays on the loading screen when deployed on our server
case.body: The app opens on my own machine, but on the server it stays on the loading screen ("Please wait...") forever. Reinstalling did not help.
case.author: reporter

evidence.title: App is not loading when running remotely
evidence.section: Symptom: the app shows "Please wait..." forever
evidence.snippet: If the page loads but stays on "Please wait...", the browser could not open the WebSocket connection to the Streamlit server. Proxies must be configured to support WebSockets.
evidence.relation: Same symptom (endless loading) and same setting (remote deployment).

evidence.title: config.toml
evidence.snippet: The URL base path to serve the app from, e.g. when the app is served under a sub-path behind a proxy.
evidence.relation: Explains a configuration needed only when the app is served under a sub-path.

evidence.title: config.toml
evidence.snippet: Enables support for Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) protection and Cross-site request forgery (XSRF) protection.
evidence.relation: Origin checks can reject the browser connection when the public URL differs from the server address.

evidence.title: (illustrative) App hangs on server after dependency upgrade
evidence.snippet: Another user fixed a hanging app by recreating the virtual environment.
evidence.relation: Similar symptom, different reporter; environment details unknown.

hypotheses.statement: A reverse proxy in front of the server does not forward WebSocket upgrade headers, so the frontend never connects to /_stcore/stream.
The app is served under a sub-path without setting server.baseUrlPath, so frontend requests go to the wrong URL.
CORS/XSRF protection rejects the browser connection because the public origin differs from the server address.
The server's Python environment is broken (dependency conflict), so the app never finishes starting.
